Question 1
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[2−3]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=b1−2b2 and c2=b1+b2?

a
[x]C=[53−43]
b
[x]C=[5313]
c
[x]C=[−2353]
d
[x]C=[13−23]
e
[x]C=[−53−23]
Submit

decision.explanation: Write x=u c₁+v c₂=(u+v)b₁+(-2u+v)b₂. Thus u+v=2 and -2u+v=-3. Subtracting gives 3u=5, so u=5/3 and v=1/3.

after.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=3{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-2{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-3(-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{c}_{2}+{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

Question 1

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[2−3]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=b1−2b2 and c2=b1+b2?

a
[x]C=[53−43]
b
[x]C=[5313]
c
[x]C=[−2353]
d
[x]C=[13−23]
e
[x]C=[−53−23]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=b1−2b2c2=b1+b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. Multiplying the second equation by 2 and adding the equations, we get

c1+2c2=3b1⟹b1=13c1+23c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=(13c1+23c2)−2b2⟹b2=−13c1+13c2.

Since [x]B=[2−3], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=2b1−3b2=2(13c1+23c2)−3(−13c1+13c2)=23c1+43c2+c1−c2=53c1+13c2

Therefore, [x]C=[5313].

content.knowledge_point: Writing a Vector in a Different Basis Given a Linear Relationship Between Two Bases
content.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
content.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=3{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-2{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-3(-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{c}_{2}+{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

after.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=3{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}={c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-5{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =-5({c}_{2}-2{c}_{1})+2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}) \\  & =-5{c}_{2}+10{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{3} \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

content.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+6(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}={c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-5{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =-5({c}_{2}-2{c}_{1})+2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}) \\  & =-5{c}_{2}+10{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{3} \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

Question 3

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[15−2418]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=3b2, c2=−6b3 and c3=3b1?

a
[x]C=[−35−8]
b
[x]C=[−8−35]
c
[x]C=[−583]
d
[x]C=[546]
e
[x]C=[3−63]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[15−2418], we can write x as follows:

x=15b1−24b2+18b3=−24b2+18b3+15b1=−8(3b2)−3(−6b3)+5(3b1)=−8c1−3c2+5c3

Therefore, [x]C=[−8−35].

decision.explanation: We have x=2b₁+2b₂+8b₃=c₂+4c₃+2c₁. In the ordered basis C, the coordinates are therefore (2,1,4), which is option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}},$ where ${c}_{1}=4{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}+8{b}_{3} \\  & =8{b}_{3}+2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =2(4{b}_{3})+2{b}_{1}+2\cdot 2(\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+4{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Writing a Three-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis
content.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}},$ where ${c}_{1}=4{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}?$
content.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}+8{b}_{3} \\  & =8{b}_{3}+2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =2(4{b}_{3})+2{b}_{1}+2\cdot 2(\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+4{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Question 5
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[2−3]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=2b1+3b2 and c2=b1+2b2?

a
 [x]C=[17−2]
b
 [x]C=[7−12]
c
 [x]C=[2−7]
d
[x]C=[3−2]
e
 [x]C=[4−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Write x=u c₁+v c₂. Matching B-coordinates gives 2u+v=2 and 3u+2v=−3. Substituting v=2−2u yields u=7 and v=−12. Indeed, 7c₁−12c₂=2b₁−3b₂.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $-2$ and adding the equations, we get  

$$
{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2})-3(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2} \\  & =7{c}_{1}-12{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -12\end{aligned}].$

content.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}?$
content.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $-2$ and adding the equations, we get  

$$
{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2})-3(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2} \\  & =7{c}_{1}-12{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -12\end{aligned}].$
